translation: Now wine is greatly hot and poisonous; in qi and flavor both it is yang; it is a thing without form. If [one] is injured by it, [one] should only diffuse and issue, and when perspiration issues [the disease] is cured — this is the most excellent method. Next to it, nothing surpasses promoting urination. These two are the separate dispersal of its dampness above and below; what then is there of wine disease? The wine-disease [sufferers] of today often take the greatly hot medicament Jiu Zheng Wan to drain down, and some use qian niu [and] da huang to drain down — this is [injury by a thing] without form, the Original Qi receiving the disease, on the contrary draining down the formed yin blood; the error is very great. Wine's nature is greatly hot; it has already injured the Original Qi and one again heavily drains it; moreover, also damaging the true yin of the kidney water, and both becoming insufficient with the formed yin blood — being so, the yin blood becomes the more vacuous, the true water the more weakened, and the poison-heat of the yang toxin greatly flourishes, on the contrary augmenting its yin fire. This is called the Original Qi disappearing and perishing, with the seven spirits having nothing on which to rely, cutting short a person's long life. If not so, then the disease of vacuity depletion is completed. The Jinkui Yaolue states: "[In] wine jaundice, [if one] drains it, for long [it becomes] black jaundice." One must be careful not to violate this admonition. It is not as good as causing its dampness to be separately dispersed above and below; Ge Hua Jie Xing Tang governs. [Note: the title in the source reads 解醒/解酲 both meaning 'to sober up from drink.']
